title: A comparison of Google One's AI Pro and Basic plans
content_html:
Published Nov 23, 2026, 7:01 PM EST

Jon Gilbert is a technology journalist with five years of experience covering mobile technology. He's covered smartwatches, tablets, smartphones, and Android accessories. He's attended CES to explore unique hardware like the Pebble Round 2 or Mudita Kompakt. His daily mobile tech life revolves around Pixel devices, which he has used since the Pixel 2 XL. Jon loves exploring the latest Android features, but is highly sceptical of anything related to AI. 

After I bought my Google Pixel 10 Pro last year, I noticed that I had been offered a free year of Google One's AI Pro plan. Perhaps the fact that I didn't notice it for a month shows how little I needed it, but the expiration date is fast approaching.

The Google AI Pro plan costs $20 a month. After my free trial is up, I will downgrade to the $2 a month Basic plan. In nearly a year of using AI Pro, I've accepted that it's almost totally worthless.

5TB is more storage than I'll ever need

I barely need 100GB

I've been taking photos and videos and storing them in Google Photos continuously since 2015. I'm not an enthusiastic photographer, but I've taken more photos in that time than I could ever possibly hope to review.

At the time of writing, I have used 76GB of my 5TB Google One storage allowance. 71GB of that is my photos and videos.

I take care to regularly clear my phone's storage of unwanted photos and back up those I want to keep.

I don't carefully manage my Google Photos storage because I don't need to worry about it. I clear out a gigabyte of photos and videos every few weeks, but I don't need to worry about forgetting.

After 11 years, I've used 71GB. At this rate, I won't need to worry about a serious cleanup until 2030 if I stick with the Basic plan, which comes with 100GB of storage.

Careful storage management makes the 5TB of storage AI Pro provides me with irrelevant.

What do I do with all this Gemini?

Nothing, that's what

Thanks to my AI Pro plan, I have access to Gemini in Gmail, Docs, Slides, Meet, and Vids. I've never felt the need to use them.

Writing AI-drafted emails feels insulting to the recipient, and I have a personal and professional ban on using AI to help me write.

It's the same story for all integrations. The Gemini features provided with AI Pro could be useful for someone with an overflowing inbox, a complete inability to write, and an aversion to Google Images.

For me, though, an ordinary bloke, it's completely useless. I don't even like the enhanced video quality in Meet, thanks to the slightly uncanny filter it lays over my video feed.

The Premium features are just as disappointing

Why can't Google bundle One with its useful services?

If Google wanted to make AI Pro more attractive, it would add premium access to its other services. But the ones it does include, I don't value, and the ones I use, it doesn't include.

YouTube Premium Lite is a nice touch, but it's not available during my trial. I'm not paying $20 on the off chance it might be worth it.

Google Home Premium and Google Health Premium are equally unhelpful. Gemini is still less useful than Assistant, and Health Premium doesn't help me.

A complete YouTube Premium and YouTube Music subscription included in the price would tempt me. Instead, Google only includes its most useless plans.

For people with smart devices embedded in every part of their home life, and those looking to maximize their fitness gains, these subscriptions are helpful. But for an unremarkable bloke like me? I don't get them.

The Basic plan provides me with everything I need

Storage is everything

For $2 a month, I get 100GB of storage with Google One's Basic plan.

Perfect.

I like the idea of bundling benefits, and I would happily pay more for a subscription that packages other useful Google features together. YouTube Premium and expanded access to Gemini Notebook would be brilliant.

But the AI Pro plan feels less like a way to bundle together Google's best features at a lower price and more like a way for Google to force us to start using its AI services.

That would be fine in theory, but the price outweighs the value. I'm not spending $240 a year on features I struggle to use.

Google's not the only one experimenting with how much we'll accept for AI features. Samsung is finally ending free access to Galaxy AI, and just like AI Pro, there's no reason for me to pay for Galaxy AI.

I'll save $18 a month by losing access to features I don't use

While I still have two months to go before I lose access to AI Pro, I've already instructed Google to return me to the Basic plan when it expires.

I'll consider paying more if Google adds more value, but until then I'll stick with my 100GB of storage.

content_html_zh:
Published Nov 23, 2026, 7:01 PM EST

Jon Gilbert is a technology journalist with five years of experience covering mobile technology. He's covered smartwatches, tablets, smartphones, and Android accessories. He's attended CES to explore unique hardware like the Pebble Round 2 or Mudita Kompakt. His daily mobile tech life revolves around Pixel devices, which he has used since the Pixel 2 XL. Jon loves exploring the latest Android features, but is highly sceptical of anything related to AI.

After I bought my Google Pixel 10 Pro last year, I noticed that I had been offered a free year of Google One's AI Pro plan. Perhaps the fact that I didn't notice it for a month shows how little I needed it, but the expiration date is fast approaching.

The Google AI Pro plan costs $20 a month. After my free trial is up, I will downgrade to the $2 a month Basic plan. In nearly a year of using AI Pro, I've accepted that it's almost totally worthless.

5TB is more storage than I'll ever need

I barely need 100GB

I've been taking photos and videos and storing them in Google Photos continuously since 2015. I'm not an enthusiastic photographer, but I've taken more photos in that time than I could ever possibly hope to review.

At the time of writing, I have used 76GB of my 5TB Google One storage allowance. 71GB of that is my photos and videos.

I take care to regularly clear my phone's storage of unwanted photos and back up those I want to keep.

I don't carefully manage my Google Photos storage because I don't need to worry about it. I clear out a gigabyte of photos and videos every few weeks, but I don't need to worry about forgetting.

After 11 years, I've used 71GB. At this rate, I won't need to worry about a serious cleanup until 2030 if I stick with the Basic plan, which comes with 100GB of storage.

Careful storage management makes the 5TB of storage AI Pro provides me with irrelevant.

What do I do with all this Gemini?

Nothing, that's what

Thanks to my AI Pro plan, I have access to Gemini in Gmail, Docs, Slides, Meet, and Vids. I've never felt the need to use them.

Writing AI-drafted emails feels insulting to the recipient, and I have a personal and professional ban on using AI to help me write.

It's the same story for all integrations. The Gemini features provided with AI Pro could be useful for someone with an overflowing inbox, a complete inability to write, and an aversion to Google Images.

For me, though, an ordinary bloke, it's completely useless. I don't even like the enhanced video quality in Meet, thanks to the slightly uncanny filter it lays over my video feed.

The Premium features are just as disappointing

Why can't Google bundle One with its useful services?

If Google wanted to make AI Pro more attractive, it would add premium access to its other services. But the ones it does include, I don't value, and the ones I use, it doesn't include.

YouTube Premium Lite is a nice touch, but it's not available during my trial. I'm not paying $20 on the off chance it might be worth it.

Google Home Premium and Google Health Premium are equally unhelpful. Gemini is still less useful than Assistant, and Health Premium doesn't help me.

A complete YouTube Premium and YouTube Music subscription included in the price would tempt me. Instead, Google only includes its most useless plans.

For people with smart devices embedded in every part of their home life, and those looking to maximize their fitness gains, these subscriptions are helpful. But for an unremarkable bloke like me? I don't get them.

The Basic plan provides me with everything I need

Storage is everything

For $2 a month, I get 100GB of storage with Google One's Basic plan.

完美的。

I like the idea of bundling benefits, and I would happily pay more for a subscription that packages other useful Google features together. YouTube Premium and expanded access to Gemini Notebook would be brilliant.

But the AI Pro plan feels less like a way to bundle together Google's best features at a lower price and more like a way for Google to force us to start using its AI services.

That would be fine in theory, but the price outweighs the value. I'm not spending $240 a year on features I struggle to use.

Google's not the only one experimenting with how much we'll accept for AI features. Samsung is finally ending free access to Galaxy AI, and just like AI Pro, there's no reason for me to pay for Galaxy AI.

I'll save $18 a month by losing access to features I don't use

While I still have two months to go before I lose access to AI Pro, I've already instructed Google to return me to the Basic plan when it expires.

I'll consider paying more if Google adds more value, but until then I'll stick with my 100GB of storage.
